Intermittent demand profiling map

The profiler classifies each time series by demand intermittency and volatility: CV2 on the x-axis, ADI on the y-axis, and SDDI on the z-axis. This helps separate regular series from spikes, lumpy, erratic, constant, and unforecastable profiles before clustering regular series with K-Means.

CV2
Coefficient of Variation Squared: demand-size volatility for non-zero demand periods. Higher CV2 means the quantity varies more when demand occurs.
ADI
Average Inter-demand Interval: average number of periods between demand occurrences. Higher ADI means demand arrives less frequently.
SDDI
Standard Deviation of Inter-demand Interval: volatility in the timing between demand events. Higher SDDI means the occurrence pattern itself is harder to forecast.

Actuals plus forecasts

Forecast values are the persisted aggregate pipeline outputs. Actuals are aggregated from the prepared weekly store data.
